content.text:
Context: this is the `obsidian-true-outliner` Obsidian plugin repo. Its e2e suite (`e2e/specs/*.e2e.ts`, run via WebdriverIO + `wdio-obsidian-service`) launches a real Obsidian Electron app per spec file. `scripts/run-e2e.mjs` is the normal entry point (`node scripts/run-e2e.mjs [desktop|mobile] [--group <name>]`) — it rebuilds the plugin, regenerates a generated hub fixture, snapshots/restores vault drift, then invokes `wdio run <config> --spec <file> --spec <file> ...` for every file in the named group (groups are decade-based prefixes on the two-digit spec filename, see `scripts/spec-groups.mjs`). A full group run of the `backlinks` group (10 files, prefixes 70-79) takes ~4 minutes and pops a real, focus-stealing Obsidian window for each spec file in sequence.

During a long review-fixing session today, the pattern that caused hours of pain: make a one-line fix, then re-run the WHOLE group to verify it and to run the negative control, because there was no fast documented way to run just the one changed test. Discovered mid-session (not documented anywhere): calling wdio directly bypasses the group wrapper's rebuild/hub-gen/drift-snapshot overhead and lets you target one file plus one test name:

```
node_modules/.bin/wdio run e2e/wdio.conf.mts --spec e2e/specs/77-footer-controls.e2e.ts --mochaOpts.grep "test name substring"
```

This took most single-test iterations from ~4 minutes to ~10-30 seconds. But it's an undocumented, manually-typed incantation, it still pops the Obsidian window, and when a FULL group run fails you still can't tell which test failed without scrolling raw stdout or re-running narrower — there's no structured "here's what failed" output.

Please do the following, using this session's real experience as the design input (don't design from scratch — read `e2e/wdio.conf.mts`, `e2e/wdio.shared.mts`, `e2e/wdio.mobile-emulation.conf.mts`, `scripts/run-e2e.mjs`, `scripts/spec-groups.mjs`, and the `obsidian` reporter config in the wdio configs first, to understand what's actually there):

1. **A documented, first-class "narrow mode" for active development.** Wrap the direct-wdio incantation discovered above into a proper script or npm script (e.g. `npm run e2e:narrow -- <file-or-group-substring> <test-name-grep>` or similar — your call on the best ergonomics), and document it prominently (README or a CLAUDE.md note, or both) as THE way to iterate on one test during development, with `scripts/run-e2e.mjs`'s full-group behavior reserved for a final check before commit/push and for CI. Make sure it still does the minimum necessary setup (plugin build at least) without the full hub-regen/drift-snapshot overhead when that's not needed — check whether those steps are actually required for the specific spec being narrowed to, or can be skipped/made conditional.

2. **Container-based e2e with Xvfb, so the window never appears at all.** Investigate whether `obsidian-launcher` (used by `wdio-obsidian-service`) supports fetching a Linux build of Obsidian (AppImage or similar), and if so, build a Docker setup (Dockerfile + compose or a run script) that runs the e2e suite inside a Linux container under Xvfb — a virtual framebuffer with no physical display, so nothing pops up on the host regardless of how many spec files run. Docker Desktop on macOS runs a Linux VM under the hood, so this is achievable from the user's Mac. Design the grouping/parallelization for this container path with the STARTUP COST in mind — spinning up a container plus Xvfb plus an Obsidian instance has fixed overhead per invocation, so batch multiple spec files per container invocation rather than one container per file, and figure out a sensible instance-count default balancing container resource limits against wall-clock time. Document how to invoke it and how it relates to the existing `E2E_MAX_INSTANCES` mechanism (`e2e/wdio.shared.mts`).

3. **Make CI the source of truth for full-suite validation, and say so explicitly in the workflow docs.** The local dev loop should not need a full green group run before every push — that's what CI's matrix (one job per group, see `.github/workflows/*` and `scripts/spec-groups.mjs`'s `--list-groups`) is for. Update whatever local process docs exist (CLAUDE.md, README, or wherever the apply-change workflow is documented) to state this plainly, so a future session doesn't reflexively re-run the whole suite locally out of caution.

4. **Structured failure reporting so a failed group run names its failure without a re-run.** Right now diagnosing "a slow group ran, one test failed, but which one and why" requires re-running narrower and grepping stdout. Look at the `obsidian` reporter currently configured (`reporters: ['obsidian']` in the wdio configs) and evaluate: can WDIO be configured with an additional reporter (e.g., `spec` with better failure formatting, or a JSON/JUnit reporter) that writes a small structured summary file (failed test names + their error messages + which spec file) that can be `cat`'d or `jq`'d after ANY run, full-group or narrow, without needing to scroll or re-run? This is the single highest-leverage fix for the "constant issue" the user named — prioritize it if time is limited.

Do this as real, working, tested infrastructure — not a proposal document. Verify each piece actually works (run a narrow test through the new tooling, run the container path if you build it, confirm the structured failure report actually appears and is useful on both a passing and a deliberately-broken test). This is infrastructure work on the harness itself, not a plugin feature — it should not touch `src/plugin/` or `openspec/` change artifacts at all. Follow the same rigor conventions as the rest of the repo (measure rather than assume, e.g. actually check whether a Linux Obsidian build is fetchable before promising the container path works, and say so plainly if it turns out not to be feasible rather than shipping something broken).
I'll start by reading the existing e2e infrastructure to understand what's actually there before designing anything.

1	/**
2	 * The logical groups the e2e specs are split into for CI.
3	 *
4	 * A group is derived from a spec's numeric prefix, so adding a spec never
5	 * requires editing this file or the workflow: the CI matrix is built from
6	 * `--list-groups`. An unrecognised decade still gets its own group, named
7	 * after the prefix, rather than being dropped from the run.
8	 *
9	 * Groups rather than `wdio --shard x/y` — which would balance better — so
10	 * that a failing check names what broke. Within-group imbalance is absorbed
11	 * by E2E_MAX_INSTANCES instead.
12	 */
13	
14	import { readdirSync } from 'node:fs';
15	import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
16	import * as path from 'node:path';
17	
18	const root = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..');
19	export const SPEC_DIR = path.join(root, 'e2e', 'specs');
20	
21	/** Prefix -> check name. A two-digit key wins over its decade, which is how a
22	 * single spec is lifted into a group of its own. */
23	const LABELS = {
24	  0: 'smoke',
25	  1: 'outline-mode',
26	  2: 'structural-commands',
27	  3: 'keyboard-grammar',
28	  4: 'shell',
29	  5: 'decorations',
30	  6: 'selection',
31	  7: 'backlinks',
32	  // Its own group: the longest spec in the suite, and its own feature.
33	  55: 'position-indicators',
34	  // Lifted out of `selection` and run one-at-a-time: see EXCLUSIVE_GROUPS.
35	  61: 'clipboard',
36	  62: 'clipboard',
37	  67: 'clipboard',
38	};
39	
40	/**
41	 * Groups whose specs contend for a resource the MACHINE owns, and so cannot run
42	 * beside each other however many instances the runner is given.
43	 *
44	 * `clipboard` is the only one. `pasteText` writes the system clipboard and then
45	 * presses Mod+V, and 61 and 67 press Mod+C into that same system clipboard —
46	 * one clipboard per machine, three specs, and workers interleaving freely.
47	 * Observed twice on CI, in both directions: a paste receiving another spec's
48	 * copied fixture, and a copy losing its content before the spec could read it.
49	 *
50	 * Serialising them is the fix that keeps the tests honest. The tempting
51	 * alternative — synthesising a `paste` ClipboardEvent so no OS clipboard is
52	 * involved — would stop exercising a real paste, and the copy side cannot be
53	 * faked that way at all.
54	 *
55	 * Only these three are serialised, so the rest of `selection` keeps its
56	 * parallelism, and the new group is a CI job of its own (the matrix is built
57	 * from `--list-groups`) which runs alongside the others anyway.
58	 */
59	export const EXCLUSIVE_GROUPS = new Set(['clipboard']);
60	
61	/**
62	 * Every spec as `{ [groupName]: absolutePath[] }`, ordered by prefix. A spec
63	 * not starting with two digits lands in `ungrouped`, so it still runs.
64	 */
65	export function specGroups() {
66	  const groups = new Map();
67	  for (const file of readdirSync(SPEC_DIR).sort()) {
68	    if (!file.endsWith('.e2e.ts')) continue;
69	    const prefix = /^(\d\d)-/.exec(file)?.[1];
70	    const decade = prefix?.[0];
71	    const name =
72	      prefix === undefined ? 'ungrouped' : (LABELS[prefix] ?? LABELS[decade] ?? `${decade}x`);
73	    if (!groups.has(name)) groups.set(name, []);
74	    groups.get(name).push(path.join(SPEC_DIR, file));
75	  }
76	  return Object.fromEntries(groups);
77	}

name: Run an e2e group
description: >
  Builds the plugin and runs one logical group of e2e specs under a cached
  Obsidian, uploading failure screenshots when the group fails.

inputs:
  node-version:

  using: composite
  steps:
    - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
      with:
        node-version: ${{ inputs.node-version }}
        cache: npm

    - run: npm ci
      shell: bash

    # Caches the downloaded Obsidian app+installer used by
    # wdio-obsidian-service. The key includes the requested version so two
    # matrix entries keep separate caches. `latest` is a moving target, so it
    # also carries the week: on a hit actions/cache does not save, meaning a
    # newly-released Obsidian would be re-downloaded on every run forever
    # without something to roll the key over. restore-keys still gives a warm
    # start from the previous week's cache.
    - id: cache-key
      run: echo "week=$(date -u +%Y-W%V)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      shell: bash

    - uses: actions/cache@v6
      with:
        path: .obsidian-cache
        key: obsidian-cache-${{ runner.os }}-${{ inputs.obsidian-version }}-${{ steps.cache-key.outputs.week }}
        restore-keys: |
          obsidian-cache-${{ runner.os }}-${{ inputs.obsidian-version }}-

    - run: npm run build:plugin
      shell: bash

    # Obsidian is an Electron app and needs a display even "headless" in CI.
    # OBSIDIAN_VERSION is read by e2e/obsidian-target.mts, which also prints the
    # resolved target and fails fast if a pinned version is not in the cache.
    - run: |
        args=()
        if [ -n "$GROUP" ]; then args+=(--group "$GROUP"); fi
        start=$SECONDS
        # `shell: bash` runs under `-e`, which would skip the timing line on a
        # failing suite — the run we most want the number for.
        set +e
        xvfb-run --auto-servernum node scripts/run-e2e.mjs "$PLATFORM" "${args[@]}"
        status=$?
        set -e
        # Header included every time: each job writes its own summary, so a
        # bare row would not render as a table.
        {
          echo "| platform | group | instances | obsidian | duration |"
          echo "|---|---|---|---|---|"
          echo "| $PLATFORM | ${GROUP:-all} | $E2E_MAX_INSTANCES | $OBSIDIAN_VERSION | $((SECONDS - start))s |"
        } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
        exit $status
      shell: bash
      env:
        GROUP: ${{ inputs.group }}
        PLATFORM: ${{ inputs.platform }}
        OBSIDIAN_VERSION: ${{ inputs.obsidian-version }}
        E2E_MAX_INSTANCES: ${{ inputs.max-instances }}

    - if: failure()
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
      with:
        name: failure-screenshots-${{ inputs.platform }}-${{ inputs.group || 'all' }}-${{ inputs.obsidian-version }}-${{ inputs.max-instances }}
        path: .obsidian-cache/failure-screenshots/
        if-no-files-found: ignore
        retention-days: 7

# @wdio/xvfb

A standalone utility to manage Xvfb (X Virtual Framebuffer) for headless testing on Linux systems.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @wdio/xvfb
```

## Usage

### Automatic Integration

**Most users don't need to use this package directly.** It's automatically integrated into:

- **`@wdio/local-runner`** - Automatically ensures xvfb is available for headless browser testing
- **`@wdio/electron-service`** - Provides headless Electron testing capabilities

Simply run your WebDriverIO tests normally, and xvfb will be managed automatically when needed.

### Manual Usage (Advanced)

For custom integrations or non-WDIO environments:

```js
import { xvfb } from "@wdio/xvfb";

// Initialize xvfb-run (only works on Linux in headless environments)
const ready = await xvfb.init();

if (ready) {
    console.log("xvfb-run is ready for use");
    // Use xvfb-run to execute commands that need a display
    // e.g., xvfb-run npm test
}
```

## API

### XvfbManager Class

#### Constructor Options

```ts
interface XvfbOptions {
    enabled?: boolean;         // Authoritative usage toggle (default: true). If false, never uses Xvfb
    force?: boolean;           // Force Xvfb even on non-Linux systems (for testing)
    autoInstall?: boolean;     // Enable automatic installation of xvfb-run if missing (default: false)
    autoInstallMode?: 'root' | 'sudo'; // Installation mode when autoInstall is true (default: 'sudo')
    autoInstallCommand?: string | string[]; // Custom installation command (overrides built-in package manager detection)
    xvfbMaxRetries?: number;   // Number of retry attempts for xvfb failures (default: 3)
    xvfbRetryDelay?: number;   // Base delay between retries in milliseconds (default: 1000)
}
```

#### Methods

-   **`shouldRun(capabilities?): boolean`** - Check if Xvfb should run on this system
-   **`init(capabilities?): Promise<boolean>`** - Initialize xvfb-run, returns true if ready, false if not needed
-   **`executeWithRetry<T>(commandFn, context?): Promise<T>`** - Execute a function with automatic retry on xvfb-related errors

### Advanced Usage Examples

#### Force Mode (Testing Only)

For testing on non-Linux systems:

```js
import { XvfbManager } from "@wdio/xvfb";

const manager = new XvfbManager({
    force: true,
    xvfbMaxRetries: 3,
    xvfbRetryDelay: 1000
});
const ready = await manager.init();
```

If you want to support the project or have opinions on the direction, please open a [discussion](https://github.com/laughedelic/obsidian-true-outliner/discussions).

## Vision

- Outliner apps (Workflowy, Roam, Logseq, Tana) share one invariant: the document is a **tree of nodes**, and every operation (typing, selecting, deleting, moving, pasting) respects **node boundaries**. The structure can't be malformed.
- Obsidian's markdown lists don't have that invariant.
  - Existing outliner plugins bolt keyboard tricks onto flat text, so the structure is one careless selection away from breaking.
  - This is fragile: the cursor has to be in just the right place, and copying or moving things around often breaks the file.
- True Outliner aims to bring the enforced-tree invariant to Obsidian without leaving markdown behind.
  - Any note is an outline: every note already has a block structure (headings, paragraphs, list items), and that structure maps losslessly onto a node tree.
  - The plugin lets you view and edit that tree directly, with the same guarantees as a dedicated outliner.
  - The file on disk stays plain, readable markdown, so it still works with every other tool, plugin, and sync method Obsidian offers.

## Goals

- Structural integrity: no operation can produce broken indentation, orphaned children, or text floating outside the tree. This is enforced, not best-effort.
- Lossless, isomorphic markdown mapping: the block tree and its markdown encoding are two views of the same thing.
  - Parsing and re-encoding a file round-trips byte-for-byte.
  - Every structural edit resolves to a well-defined, minimal diff, never hidden state, never a lossy rewrite of the whole file.
- Any note, not a special mode: the outliner isn't a separate note type or a vault takeover, it's a way of looking at and editing the notes you already have.
- Public APIs only: built on Obsidian's documented editor and plugin APIs, no monkey-patching private internals, so it stays compatible and passes the community plugin safety bar honestly.
- Clean files: no required front matter, IDs, or metadata just to make the outliner work. What the outliner needs to track (like fold state) lives in plugin data, not in your notes.

## Approach

- The design splits into two layers:
  - A pure mapping core: markdown parsing, encoding, and structural operations (indent, outdent, move, etc.) as a standalone library with no editor or Obsidian dependency. Correctness here (round-tripping, op closure, minimal edits) is verified independently of any UI.
  - An editor integration: a CodeMirror 6 extension inside Obsidian's standard markdown view that renders and drives that model, giving the outliner experience without replacing the file format or the editor.
- The mapping algebra has two structural regimes:
  - Headings behave like org-mode promote/demote: indent/outdent shifts heading level.
  - Everything else reparents relative to siblings, with markdown encoding recomputed from context.
  - Either way, an operation produces a well-formed tree, or it's rejected with a clear, typed reason, never a partial or ambiguous result.
- The research and design decisions behind these choices are written up in [docs/research/](docs/research/).

# Runs the e2e suite headlessly on Linux, under Xvfb, so the Obsidian window
# that `scripts/run-e2e.mjs` pops on a real display never appears at all — see
# `e2e/docker/README.md` for how to invoke this and why.
#
# `node:26-bookworm` (not `-slim`) rather than a from-scratch Debian install:
# CI already proves this shape works (`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs
# `ubuntu-latest` + Node 26 + `xvfb-run`), so this mirrors a configuration
# already known to launch Obsidian, and the non-slim base carries more of the
# shared libraries Electron needs out of the box.
FROM node:26-bookworm

# The library set below is what an Electron app (Obsidian, via
# obsidian-launcher) needs to start under Xvfb on Debian — confirmed by
# actually building this image and running the suite inside it (see the
# README), not copied from an unverified list.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    xvfb \
    xauth \
    dbus \
    libnss3 \
    libatk1.0-0 \
    libatk-bridge2.0-0 \
    libcups2 \
    libdrm2 \
    libxkbcommon0 \
    libxcomposite1 \
    libxdamage1 \
    libxfixes3 \
    libxrandr2 \
    libgbm1 \
    libpango-1.0-0 \
    libcairo2 \
    libasound2 \
    libgtk-3-0 \
    fonts-liberation \
  && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

WORKDIR /workspace

# Dependencies are baked into the image at build time (Linux binaries for
# esbuild, Electron, etc). The compose file mounts a named volume over
# node_modules at runtime instead of the host's node_modules, which never
# has Linux binaries on a macOS/Windows host — see e2e/docker/README.md.
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci

COPY . .

CMD ["bash"]

 * A git WORKTREE's `.git` is a file pointing at an absolute host path
 * (`<main checkout>/.git/worktrees/<name>`) — bind-mounting the worktree
 * alone gives the container that pointer with nothing at the far end, so
 * every git-invoking step (the build stamp in esbuild.config.mjs, and
 * `git status`/`checkout` in scripts/check-vault-drift.mjs) fails with "not
 * a git repository".
 *
 * Bind-mounting the real git dir at the SAME absolute path — the more
 * obvious fix — does not work here: this host (OrbStack) silently fails a
 * bind mount whose source and target path are identical, confirmed with a
 * plain `docker run -v $P:$P alpine ls $P` before reaching for this. So
 * instead the git dir is mounted at an arbitrary container path and
 * `GIT_COMMON_DIR`/`GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` point git at it directly,
 * bypassing `.git`-file resolution entirely — verified against `git status`
 * and `git rev-parse` inside the container, not just rev-parse alone, since
 * check-vault-drift.mjs needs the former.
 *
 * A plain (non-worktree) checkout's `--git-common-dir` is just `.git` under
 * the already-mounted root, so this is a no-op there.
 */
function gitVolumeAndEnvArgs() {
  const commonDir = path.resolve(
    root,
    execFileSync('git', ['rev-parse', '--git-common-dir'], { cwd: root, encoding: 'utf-8' }).trim(),
  );
  if (commonDir === path.join(root, '.git')) return [];

  const gitDir = path.resolve(
    root,
    execFileSync('git', ['rev-parse', '--absolute-git-dir'], { cwd: root, encoding: 'utf-8' }).trim(),
  );
  const relativeGitDir = path.relative(commonDir, gitDir); // e.g. worktrees/<name>
  return [
    '-v',
    `${commonDir}:/git-common:ro`,
    '-e',
    'GIT_COMMON_DIR=/git-common',
    '-e',
    `GIT_DIR=/git-common/${relativeGitDir}`,
    '-e',
    'GIT_WORK_TREE=/workspace',
  ];
}

# Headless e2e (Docker + Xvfb)

`scripts/run-e2e.mjs` and `scripts/e2e-narrow.mjs` both launch a real Obsidian window on
macOS/Windows — CI runs the same suite headlessly on Linux under Xvfb
(`.github/workflows/ci.yml` uses `xvfb-run` on `ubuntu-latest`), which is what this reproduces
locally, so a run — narrow, grouped, or full — never has to pop a window on the host.

## Invoke

```bash
npm run test:e2e:docker                    # whole suite, desktop
npm run test:e2e:docker -- --group smoke   # one CI-style group
npm run test:e2e:docker:mobile             # mobile-emulation config
```

Both wrap `scripts/e2e-docker.mjs`, which drives `docker compose` (`docker-compose.yml` in this
directory) — don't invoke `docker compose` directly, the script also validates `--group` against
`scripts/spec-groups.mjs` and works out the worktree git-dir handling described below.

The image builds automatically on first run (and on any later `Dockerfile`/`package.json`
change, via Docker's own layer cache) — pass `--build` to force a rebuild.

## What's actually verified, not assumed

Built from `node:26-bookworm` (matching CI's Node version) plus the Debian packages an Electron
app needs to start under Xvfb — arrived at by building this image and running the suite inside
it, not copied from an unverified list. `obsidian-launcher` (the package `wdio-obsidian-service`
uses to fetch Obsidian) does support a Linux target — confirmed by watching it fetch and launch
one inside the container, the same way CI already does on `ubuntu-latest`.

## Design choices

**One container per invocation**, covering however many specs are in scope — the whole suite by
default, or one group with `--group`. Never one container per spec file: `scripts/run-e2e.mjs`
inside the container already dispatches every spec in scope through a single wdio run,
parallelised across `E2E_MAX_INSTANCES` workers, so batching multiple files per container
invocation is inherited from the existing script rather than reimplemented here. This
deliberately does not fan out multiple containers to run several groups in parallel the way CI's
matrix does — CI already gives full-suite, parallel-across-groups coverage (see AGENTS.md's "E2E
testing" section), so this path's job is a headless run, not a faster one.

`E2E_MAX_INSTANCES` defaults to **2** for the container (`scripts/e2e-docker.mjs`), lower than
CI's `max-instances: 4`: a CI runner is dedicated to the job, while this container shares the
Docker Desktop/OrbStack Linux VM's CPU allocation with everything else on the host. Override with
`E2E_MAX_INSTANCES=N npm run test:e2e:docker`; `docker info` reports what the VM currently has to
give.

**Dependencies are installed at image build time**, not on every run: `npm ci` happens inside the
`Dockerfile`, baking Linux binaries (esbuild, etc.) into the image. At runtime, `docker-compose.yml`
mounts a *named volume* over `/workspace/node_modules`, shadowing the bind-mounted repo's
`node_modules` — otherwise a macOS/Windows host's `node_modules` (wrong-platform native binaries)
would sit in front of the image's. Docker seeds a fresh named volume from the image's content at
that path the first time it's used, so this needs no extra setup step. A second named volume
persists `.obsidian-cache` (the downloaded Obsidian build, ~150-250MB) across runs.

**Rebuild the image or drop the `e2e-node-modules` volume** after a dependency change that isn't
reflected in a rebuild for some reason: `docker volume rm docker_e2e-node-modules` (the exact
name is prefixed by whatever `docker compose` derives from this directory — `docker volume ls`
to check).

## Worktree caveat

A git **worktree**'s `.git` is a file pointing at an absolute host path
(`<main checkout>/.git/worktrees/<name>`) — bind-mounting the worktree alone gives the container
that pointer with nothing at the far end, and anything that shells out to git (the build stamp in
`esbuild.config.mjs`, `git status`/`checkout` in `scripts/check-vault-drift.mjs`) fails with "not
a git repository".

`scripts/e2e-docker.mjs` handles this automatically: it mounts the real git-common-dir at an
arbitrary container path and points `GIT_COMMON_DIR`/`GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` at it directly,
bypassing `.git`-file resolution. (Bind-mounting the git dir at the *same* absolute path — the
more obvious fix — silently fails on this host: OrbStack drops a bind mount whose source and
target path are identical, confirmed with a plain `docker run -v $P:$P alpine ls $P` before
reaching for the env-var approach instead.) A plain, non-worktree checkout needs none of this —
`git rev-parse --git-common-dir` is already `.git` under the mounted root.

# with that server available, and kills the X server when done.  The return
# value of the command becomes the return value of this script.
#
# If anyone is using this to build a Debian package, make sure the package
# Build-Depends on xvfb and xauth.

SERVERNUM=99
AUTHFILE=
ERRORFILE=/dev/null

LISTENTCP="-nolisten tcp"
XAUTHPROTO=.

All four pieces are built, wired together, and validated against a real running container/Obsidian instance — not just written and assumed. Summary:

**1. Narrow mode** — [scripts/e2e-narrow.mjs](scripts/e2e-narrow.mjs), `npm run test:e2e:narrow -- <spec> [grep]`. Measured the setup steps (build, hub-gen, drift-snapshot) at under 0.5s combined — they were never the bottleneck, so I kept them rather than adding speculative conditionals; the real win is targeting one spec file directly instead of a whole group. Took an iteration from minutes to ~14s in testing.

**2. Docker + Xvfb** — [e2e/docker/](e2e/docker/), `npm run test:e2e:docker[:mobile] [-- --group <name>]`. Ran the smoke group inside a real Linux/arm64 container end-to-end (`platform: linux` in the reporter output confirms it), with a deliberately-failing scratch test to prove failure detection works there too. Hit and fixed two real bugs along the way, documented in the code/README:
- `xvfb-run`'s signal-based readiness wait hung indefinitely in-container; replaced with a small script that polls for the X socket file instead.
- The worktree's `.git` pointer doesn't resolve inside the container (and this host's OrbStack silently drops same-path bind mounts); fixed via `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_COMMON_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` pointed at a differently-mounted git dir.
- A first version shadowed the whole `.obsidian-cache` with a named volume, which hid the failure summary from the host — caught it, rescoped the volume to just the binary subdirectories.

Not built: multi-container parallelism across groups. CI's matrix already covers that; documented why in the README rather than reimplementing it locally.

**3. Docs** — added an "E2E testing" section to [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) (symlinked as CLAUDE.md) stating CI is the source of truth for full-suite validation, and [e2e/docker/README.md](e2e/docker/README.md) for the container path specifics.

**4. Structured failure reporting** — added `@wdio/json-reporter` alongside the existing `obsidian` reporter in both wdio configs, with a custom `onComplete` in [e2e/wdio.shared.mts](e2e/wdio.shared.mts) that collapses every worker's dump into `.obsidian-cache/e2e-summary.json` — verified with a real pass and a real deliberate failure (`jq`-able, one stable path, works identically for narrow/grouped/full and local/container runs).

One thing I didn't run: the `:mobile` variant of the Docker path specifically (only tested `desktop`) — it's the same well-exercised code path with `OBSIDIAN_E2E_MOBILE` already handled by the unmodified `run-e2e.mjs`, so risk is low, but flagging that I didn't execute it.

1	# e2e-verification Specification
2	
3	## Purpose
4	Defines the automated end-to-end verification harness: a real (sandboxed) Obsidian
5	instance driven against a throwaway copy of `test-vault/` to exercise behavior that only
6	exists in a live app — command dispatch, keyboard grammar, on-disk byte fidelity, and
7	persistence across restarts — replacing the manual dev-vault checklist it supersedes.
8	## Requirements
9	### Requirement: Sandboxed real-Obsidian harness
10	
11	The project SHALL provide an automated end-to-end harness that launches a
12	real Obsidian instance with the built plugin installed and a throwaway copy
13	of `test-vault/`, runnable with a single command (`npm run test:e2e`). The
14	harness MUST NOT modify the checked-in `test-vault/` and MUST NOT affect the
15	plugin bundle, the vitest suite, or the plugin typecheck.
16	
17	#### Scenario: One-command run against a sandbox
18	
19	- **WHEN** a developer runs `npm run test:e2e`
20	- **THEN** the plugin is rebuilt, Obsidian launches against a sandboxed copy
21	  of `test-vault/` with the plugin enabled, all e2e specs run, and after the
22	  run `git status` shows no changes under `test-vault/`
23	
24	#### Scenario: Harness excluded from bundle and unit tests
25	
26	- **WHEN** `npm run build:plugin`, `npm test`, and `npm run build` execute
27	- **THEN** none of them compile, bundle, or run any file under `e2e/`
28	
29	### Requirement: Outline mode e2e verification
30	
31	The harness SHALL verify outline-mode lifecycle end-to-end: toggling by
32	command id shows a notice and leaves file bytes and mtime unchanged; mode
33	survives an app restart with no trace in note content; mode follows renames;
34	deletion prunes the path from plugin data; structural commands are absent on
35	non-outline notes.
36	
37	#### Scenario: Toggle leaves file untouched
38	
39	- **WHEN** the toggle command runs on an open note and the buffer is saved
40	- **THEN** a notice appears and the note's on-disk bytes and mtime equal
41	  their pre-toggle values
42	
43	#### Scenario: Mode persists across restart
44	
45	- **WHEN** outline mode is enabled for a note and Obsidian is restarted
46	  preserving state
47	- **THEN** the note is still in outline mode (grammar keys act) and its
48	  content contains no mode marker
49	
50	#### Scenario: Rename follows, delete prunes
51	
52	- **WHEN** an outline note is renamed, and separately when one is deleted
53	- **THEN** `data.json` lists the new path after rename and no longer lists
54	  the deleted path after delete
55	
56	#### Scenario: Commands gated to outline notes
57	
58	- **WHEN** command availability is checked on a non-outline note
59	- **THEN** the four structural commands report unavailable, and on an
60	  outline note they report available
61	
62	### Requirement: Structural command e2e verification
63	
64	The harness SHALL verify the four structural commands (indent, outdent,
65	move up, move down) invoked by command id against real notes: text
66	transforms match the spec'd behavior, cursor lands correctly, every accepted
67	operation is a single undo step restoring the exact prior text, and every
68	rejection shows its message while leaving the document byte-identical.
69	
70	#### Scenario: Indent/outdent round-trip with undo
71	
72	- **WHEN** a paragraph under a paragraph is indented and then outdented
73	- **THEN** it becomes a `- item` with the cursor after `- `, the outdent
74	  restores the original text exactly, and one undo keystroke reverses each
75	  step
76	
77	#### Scenario: Heading demote keeps links resolving
78

## PR

Opened as a draft: [obsidian-true-outliner#74](https://github.com/laughedelic/obsidian-true-outliner/pull/74) (`chore/e2e-dev-loop` → `main`), two commits — one for the tooling, one for the docs/config. Docs alone don't hold — anyone (agent or human) who already knows the old `npm run test:e2e -- --group X` incantation, or types the raw `wdio --spec ... --mochaOpts.grep ...` from muscle memory, just bypasses AGENTS.md entirely since nothing reads it back to them at the moment of the mistake. - **Runtime nudge in `run-e2e.mjs`** (cheapest, catches everyone): when it's about to launch more than ~2-3 spec files outside `CI=true`, print a one-line reminder pointing at `test:e2e:narrow` before proceeding. No blocking, fires exactly when the costly choice is made, works for a human in a terminal exactly as well as an agent.
- **A Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook** (agent-specific, more targeted): pattern-match the raw `wdio run ... --spec ... --mochaOpts.grep` incantation or `npm run test:e2e -- --group` in Bash calls and inject a reminder before it runs. Catches the exact bypass this session rediscovered, but only helps Claude Code sessions, adds a hook to maintain, and needs care not to nag on the legitimate "final check before a checkpoint" case.

#!/bin/sh
# Starts a virtual X server, exports DISPLAY, and execs the given command
# against it — e.g. `node scripts/run-e2e.mjs desktop` or
# `node scripts/e2e-narrow.mjs <spec>`.

# reliable readiness check here. Exporting DISPLAY before the command also
# makes @wdio/xvfb's own auto-management (used by @wdio/local-runner) a
# no-op — it only acts when DISPLAY is unset.
set -e

Xvfb :99 -screen 0 1280x1024x24 -nolisten tcp &
XVFB_PID=$!
trap 'kill $XVFB_PID 2>/dev/null' EXIT

tries=50
while [ ! -e /tmp/.X11-unix/X99 ]; do
  tries=$((tries - 1))
  if [ $tries -le 0 ]; then
    echo "[start-xvfb-and-run] Xvfb did not come up in time" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  sleep 0.2
done

export DISPLAY=:99
exec "$@"

# Headless e2e (Docker + Xvfb)

`scripts/run-e2e.mjs` and `scripts/e2e-narrow.mjs` both launch a real Obsidian window on
macOS/Windows. CI runs the same suite headlessly on Linux under Xvfb instead
(`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `ubuntu-latest`) — this reproduces that locally in a container, so a
run — narrow, grouped, or full — never has to pop a window on the host, whatever OS it runs.

## Invoke

```bash
npm run test:e2e:docker                                        # whole suite, desktop
npm run test:e2e:docker -- --group smoke                       # one CI-style group
npm run test:e2e:docker -- 77-footer-controls "renders it"     # one spec, one test (narrow mode)
npm run test:e2e:docker:mobile -- --group smoke                # mobile-emulation config
```

A bare positional argument (not `--group`'s own value) runs `scripts/e2e-narrow.mjs` inside the
container instead of `scripts/run-e2e.mjs`, the same way it would locally.

Both npm scripts wrap `scripts/e2e-docker.mjs`, which drives `docker compose`
(`docker-compose.yml` in this directory) — don't invoke `docker compose` directly, the script also
validates `--group` against `scripts/spec-groups.mjs` and works out the worktree git-dir and
host-UID handling described below.

The image is rebuilt on every invocation (`docker compose run --build`) — Docker's own per-layer
cache makes an unchanged build sub-second, so this doesn't need a separate `--build` flag or a
"did you remember to rebuild" step; `docker compose run` alone, without `--build`, would silently
keep using a stale image instead of picking up a `Dockerfile`/`package.json` change.

## What's actually verified, not assumed

Built from `node:26-bookworm` (matching CI's Node version) plus the Debian packages an Electron
app needs to start under Xvfb — arrived at by building this image and running the suite inside
it, not copied from an unverified list. `obsidian-launcher` (the package `wdio-obsidian-service`
uses to fetch Obsidian) does support a Linux target — confirmed by watching it fetch and launch
one inside the container, the same way CI already does on `ubuntu-latest`.

## Design choices

**One container per invocation**, covering however many specs are in scope — the whole suite by
default, one group with `--group`, or one spec (optionally one test) in narrow mode. Never one
container per spec file: `scripts/run-e2e.mjs`/`scripts/e2e-narrow.mjs` inside the container
already dispatch every spec in scope through a single wdio run, so batching multiple files per
container invocation is inherited from those scripts rather than reimplemented here. This
deliberately does not fan out multiple containers to run several groups in parallel the way CI's
matrix does — CI already gives full-suite, parallel-across-groups coverage (see AGENTS.md's "E2E
testing" section), so this path's job is a headless run, not a faster one.

`E2E_MAX_INSTANCES` defaults to **2** for the container (`scripts/e2e-docker.mjs`), lower than
CI's `max-instances: 4`: a CI runner is dedicated to the job, while this container shares the
Docker Desktop/OrbStack Linux VM's CPU allocation with everything else on the host. Override with
`E2E_MAX_INSTANCES=N npm run test:e2e:docker`; `docker info` reports what the VM currently has to
give.

**No `xvfb-run`.** `e2e/docker/start-xvfb-and-run.sh` starts `Xvfb` itself and polls for its
socket file before exporting `DISPLAY` and `exec`ing whatever command it's given — see that
script's header. The obvious choice, wrapping the whole invocation in `xvfb-run --auto-servernum`,
hung indefinitely in this container: `Xvfb` came up but the wrapped `node` process never started,
because the `wait`/`SIGUSR1` handshake `xvfb-run`'s own shell script uses for readiness never
completed.

**Runs as the invoking host UID/GID**, not the image's default root — `scripts/e2e-docker.mjs`
passes `-u $(uid):$(gid)` (a no-op on Windows, which has no POSIX UID/GID). On Docker
Desktop/OrbStack's VM this mostly doesn't matter, but on a native Linux host, root-owned output
from a root-run container writing into a bind-mounted, user-owned repo is a real, sticky problem:
it breaks the next host-side build, and can make git refuse the checkout as owned by someone else.
`node_modules` and the `.obsidian-cache` mount points are made world-writable in the `Dockerfile`
so an arbitrary host UID (which has no matching user in the image) can still write to them.

**Dependencies are installed at image build time**, not on every run: `npm ci` happens inside the
`Dockerfile`, baking Linux binaries (esbuild, etc.) into the image. At runtime,
`docker-compose.yml` mounts an *anonymous* volume over `/workspace/node_modules`, shadowing the
bind-mounted repo's `node_modules` — otherwise a macOS/Windows host's `node_modules`
(wrong-platform native binaries) would sit in front of the image's. Anonymous, not named: it's
re-seeded from the image on every `run`, so a `package-lock.json` change always takes effect on
the very next run. A *named* volume there — persistent across runs by design — would instead keep
serving whatever `node_modules` existed the first time it was created, no matter how many times
the image was rebuilt after.

Three *named* volumes persist what `obsidian-launcher` downloads (Obsidian itself, its installer,
and the Electron/Chromedriver build) across container runs — scoped to exactly those subdirectories
under `.obsidian-cache`, deliberately not the whole directory: `e2e-summary.json` and
`e2e-reports/` (see AGENTS.md's "E2E testing" section) land under `.obsidian-cache` too, on every
run, and need to stay on the bind-mounted host filesystem — `cat .obsidian-cache/e2e-summary.json`
right after the container exits is the whole point of that file. Shadowing the whole directory
with one volume (an earlier version of this compose file did) would make the summary invisible
outside the container.

**Drop a volume** after an Obsidian-version change that isn't reflected some other way:
`docker volume ls` to see the actual names (`docker compose` prefixes them, e.g.
`docker_e2e-obsidian-app`), `docker volume rm <name>` to drop one. `node_modules` needs no such
step — see above.

## Worktree caveat

A git **worktree**'s `.git` is a file pointing at an absolute host path
(`<main checkout>/.git/worktrees/<name>`) — bind-mounting the worktree alone gives the container
that pointer with nothing at the far end, and anything that shells out to git (the build stamp in
`esbuild.config.mjs`, `git status`/`checkout` in `scripts/check-vault-drift.mjs`) fails with "not
a git repository".

`scripts/e2e-docker.mjs` handles this automatically: it mounts the real git-common-dir read-only at
an arbitrary container path, mounts the worktree's own gitdir (nested under it) read-write on top —
cleanup's `git checkout` needs to write `index.lock` there — and points
`GIT_COMMON_DIR`/`GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` at them directly, bypassing `.git`-file resolution.
(Bind-mounting the git dir at the *same* absolute path — the more obvious fix — is not reliable:
some Docker file-sharing backends no-op a bind mount whose source and target path are identical.)
A plain, non-worktree checkout needs none of this — `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` is already
`.git` under the mounted root.
